title: Tandoori Flames Opens in Champaign With Gujarati, Bombay Chaat and Tandoor Menus
excerpt: The family-owned restaurant opened on Wednesday, November 4, at 1005 S Neil Street in the former El Toro space, serving lunch and dinner seven days a week with a limited opening menu, Smile Politely reports.
body:
• Tandoori Flames opened on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, at 1005 S Neil Street in Champaign, in the former El Toro space, starting with a limited menu and a brand-new staff, according to Smile Politely.
  • The family-owned restaurant is open for lunch and dinner seven days a week, 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. and 4:30 to 10 p.m.
  • The menu spans Gujarati food, Bombay chaat, tandoor dishes, biryani, noodles, 15 breads and 12 kinds of sandwiches, plus desserts including gulab jamun and ras malai.
  • There is no online ordering yet, so plan to walk in: the chicken curry costs $16.99 with rice and garlic naan is $4.99, per Smile Politely's opening-day visit.

Champaign has a new Indian restaurant. Tandoori Flames opened on Wednesday, November 4, at 1005 S Neil Street, taking over the former El Toro space on Neil Street, Smile Politely reported after visiting on opening day. The family-owned restaurant opened with a limited menu and a brand-new staff, and the magazine's reviewer, arriving at lunch, was its first customer.

The restaurant serves lunch and dinner seven days a week, with a break in the afternoon. The hours posted by Smile Politely are 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. and 4:30 to 10 p.m. daily.

A menu that runs wide

The menu covers appetizers, sandwiches, mains and platters, and reaches well beyond a standard curry list. Smile Politely lists Gujarati food, Bombay chaat, tandoor cooking, noodles, biryani, soups, naan, parantha and papad among the sections it saw. Additional menu pages listed vegetarian appetizers, seafood entrees and biryani specials, along with 15 breads and 12 kinds of sandwiches.

Desserts include gulab jamun, ras malai, moong dal halwa, kheer, rabdi and ice cream. Drinks include milkshakes, juices, falooda and kulfi. According to Smile Politely, the restaurant also plans to serve beer, wine and liquor in the future.

What the first taste found

Not everything on the full menu was offered on opening day, but most items were available, Smile Politely reported. The reviewer ordered the chicken curry, priced at $16.99 with rice, and garlic naan at $4.99. The curry was described as slow-cooked tomato with tender chicken and light spiciness; ordered medium, it came out milder than expected, with the reviewer planning to ask for more heat next time. The garlic naan was warm, charred and covered in minced garlic, and was recommended.

The rose falooda, at $12.99, combined rose syrup, milk, crushed pistachios, sweet basil (sabja) seeds and thin vermicelli noodles. The reviewer liked the flavours but found the drink heavily loaded with noodles.

Service on day one was quick. Smile Politely noted there is no online ordering at this time, but the restaurant has a register right inside and, in the reviewer's words, a pretty quick kitchen. Updates are posted on the restaurant's Instagram account.

Where it fits in Champaign-Urbana

Tandoori Flames joins an Indian food scene that local guide ChambanaMoms describes as being in a golden era in Central Illinois, after a period when only a couple of restaurants served Indian food in Champaign-Urbana. The guide links that growth to the many Indian students at the University of Illinois and to the Indian and Indian-American families who live in the community, and it lists established options including Kohinoor and Himalayan Chimney downtown and Signature Grill, Ambar India, Indian Chaat Cafe and Naya Indian Cuisine near campus.

Against that field, Tandoori Flames' opening-day pitch is breadth and hours: a family-owned kitchen on Neil Street, open every day for both lunch and dinner, with Gujarati and Bombay chaat sections alongside tandoor and biryani. Whether the full menu holds once the limited opening menu expands is the thing to watch, along with the planned drinks licence reported by Smile Politely.

Before you go

Tandoori Flames is at 1005 S Neil Street, Champaign, open 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. and 4:30 to 10 p.m. daily, according to Smile Politely. Because there is no online ordering yet and the restaurant opened with a limited menu, opening-week visitors should expect a shorter version of the printed menu and order at the register inside.
